item.text: I’ll read the fixture and solve the scheduling constraints with the requested tie-breakers.

item.command:
/bin/zsh -lc "python3 -c 'import json,itertools
p=json.load(open(\"input.json\")); ops=sorted(p[\"operations\"],key=lambda x:x[\"id\"]); h=p[\"horizon\"]; best=None; count=0
choices=[o[\"permitted_starts\"] if o[\"permitted_starts\"] is not None else range(h-o[\"duration\"]+1) for o in ops]
for v in itertools.product(*choices):
 s=dict(zip([o[\"id\"] for o in ops],v)); f={o[\"id\"]:s[o[\"id\"]]+o[\"duration\"] for o in ops}
 if any(f[o[\"id\"]]>h or any(f[r]>s[o[\"id\"]] for r in o[\"requires\"]) for o in ops):continue
 if any(sum(o[\"demand\"].get(k,0) for o in ops if s[o[\"id\"]]<=t<f[o[\"id\"]])>cap for t in range(h) for k,cap in p[\"capacities\"].items()):continue
 count+=1; key=(max(f.values()),sum(s[o[\"id\"]]*o[\"risk_weight\"] for o in ops),v)
 if best is None or key<best:best=key
print(json.dumps({\"starts\":dict(zip([o[\"id\"] for o in ops],best[2])),\"makespan\":best[0],\"risk_exposure\":best[1]}))
print(\"feasible schedules:\",count)'"
